name: Samba
description: Samba is a rummy card game that involves melding, sets, runs. The game originated in USA/UK and has become popular worldwide.

overview.description: Samba is a rummy card game that involves melding, sets, runs. The game originated in USA/UK and has become popular worldwide.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: USA/UK
Time Period: Early 1900s
Historical Development: The game evolved from traditional card games in the region
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

setup.players:
Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4 (partnerships)
Partnerships: With 4 or 6 players, partners sit opposite.
setup.deck: Type: Three standard 52-card decks plus 6 jokers (162 cards total). Twos and jokers are wild.
setup.dealing: Cards per Player: 15 each for 2–5 players; 13 each for 6 players. One card turned face up to start discard pile; remainder forms stock. Dealing clockwise.
setup.equipment: Three 52-card decks, 6 jokers, score sheet, table space.

rules.objective: Score points by melding groups and sequences; first team to reach 10,000 points at the end of a hand wins.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal: 15 cards each (2–5 players) or 13 each (6 players). One card up for discard pile; rest is stock.
2. Turn: Draw two from stock (or take discard pile under rules, or take one card to add to existing sequence), meld if desired, discard one.
3. Melds: Groups (3+ same rank, max 2 wilds) and sequences (3–7 same suit, no wilds). Seven-card group = canasta; seven-card sequence = samba.
4. Going out: Must have two sambas, or two canastas, or one of each; then meld all or all but one and discard the last.
5. Scoring: Card values plus bonuses (samba 1500, pure canasta 500, mixed 300, going out 200); first to 10,000 wins.
keyRules: Initial meld must meet minimum point value (50–150) by team score.
Red threes: meld for 100 bonus each if team has required sambas/canastas; else 100 penalty each.
Cannot take discard top to start a new sequence; only to add to existing sequence or to take pile with two natural match.
Black threes and wilds block discard pile when on top.

strategy.basic: Build toward two sambas or canastas; meet initial meld; avoid holding red threes if you cannot go out.
strategy.intermediate: Every samba contains 8, 9 or 10; if opponents hold canastas in those ranks in your suit, switch to canastas. Meld 8-9-10 sequences early so partner can add.
strategy.advanced: Use wilds to block discard pile when it holds cards opponents need. Red threes only pay when you have the two required sets to go out.
tips: Hand grows by one card per turn (draw two, discard one); keep black threes, twos and jokers in separate piles for clarity.
You cannot take the pile to start a new sequence; only to add to an existing sequence meld.

variations.name: Bolivia
variations.description: Similar to Samba but allows melds of seven wild cards (bolivia), worth 2500; to go out need two 7-card melds with at least one sequence (escalera).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses same deck and player count; rule differences are in meld types and going-out requirement.
